title: Component Verification Report
description: Required before a proposed component or variant (from a component-gap-report) can flip status to 'approved' in the manifest's components[] registry. Two jobs: (1) confirm it's actually operational, not just visually plausible — every state implemented, accessible, responsive; (2) explain why it was built this way, so a reviewer isn't approving a black box.

id.description: Stable ID for this report, e.g. 'DES-512-gap-1-verify'. Referenced by design-output.verificationReportsFiled.

variantName.description: Set if this verifies a variant of an existing component rather than a whole new component.

operationalSpec.description: What this component actually does — the contract a build agent or future designer can rely on without re-deriving it from the mockup.

purpose.description: One line: what this component is for and when to reach for it.

states.description: Every interaction/data state this component must handle, not just the one shown in the mockup.

description.description: What changes in this state and why.

implemented.description: Whether this state actually exists in the artifact, not just in the spec.

notApplicable.description: True when this state deliberately does not apply to the component (e.g. focus on a non-interactive display). Requires notApplicableReason. Excluded from verification.allStatesImplemented.

notApplicableReason.description: Required when notApplicable is true: why the state doesn't apply, citing the ticket, a principle, or whenNotToUse.

responsiveBehavior.description: What this component does at each layout.breakpoints step — required if it's used anywhere near a breakpoint boundary.

breakpoint.description: e.g. 'sm', 'md', or a raw px value.

whenNotToUse.description: Explicit boundary — prevents the component being reached for outside its intended purpose later.

dynamicBehavior.description: How the component adapts, per the dynamic-components rules in design-principles.md. No component is approved without it: this is what makes every component work on mobile and everywhere else.

sizing.description: How it sizes: e.g. 'fills its container; min 160px, max 320px wide; height from content'. Fixed sizes only for icons/targets up to mobile.maxFixedSizePx.

containerAdaptation.description: What it does at each container width it can be placed in, narrowest first.

long.description: Including translated text up to mobile.textExpansionPercent longer, and long unbroken words.

overflow.description: How truncated content stays reachable in full.

result.description: What changes, and confirmation nothing clips or overlaps.

orientationAndSafeArea.description: Landscape behavior, and safe-area/keyboard handling if it sits near a screen edge.

dataDriven.description: Confirms content comes in through props, with nothing hard-coded.

designRationale.description: Why this component looks and behaves the way it does — one entry per notable structural decision. Every entry must cite a principle, token, or manifest field, not a preference (same bar as implementationNote in audit-report.schema.json).

decision.description: e.g. 'Trend indicator uses an arrow icon + color, not color alone.'

reasoning.description: e.g. 'accessibility.requireSemanticHtml and rubric category 2 — color can't be the only signal for state.'

verification.description: The operational-readiness checklist — did it actually get built out, not just described.

allStatesImplemented.description: False if any state in operationalSpec.states that is not marked notApplicable has implemented: false. States marked notApplicable (with a reason) do not count against this.

accessibilityPass.description: Meets accessibility.level from the manifest — contrast, touch target, focus visibility, semantics.

dynamicPass.description: Works at the narrowest container and at mobile.minViewportPx, survives maxTextScalePercent and textExpansionPercent, handles empty content, and works by touch alone.

tokenCompliant.description: Uses only manifest tokens — no hardcoded values (design-principles.md: Consistency Is Non-Negotiable).

checkedBy.description: 'agent-self-check-pending-human' means the agent ran the checklist but a human hasn't confirmed it yet — cannot alone justify an 'approved' status if registryPolicy.verificationReviewer requires human sign-off.

verdict.description: 'ready-for-implementation' is what allows the linked component-gap-report's status to flip from 'proposed' to 'approved' in the manifest — this is the actual approval gate, not the gap report by itself.

revisionNotes.description: Required if verdict is needs-revision — specific, not general.
